paragraphs.text: Deepseek harness plugin for control rate limits
# dsh-llm-model-rate-limit
Per-model rate limits for DeepSeek Harness requests and tokens — keep your agents under provider lim
its without HTTP 429s stopping them.
## What it does
Each model (`provider/model`) gets its own budget over four rolling windows — second, minute, hour,
day — for requests and for tokens. When a model reaches a limit, the agent doesn't stop or error out
: the request waits in a FIFO queue spending zero tokens, a single timer wakes it the instant the wi
ndow frees, and the unchanged request is sent automatically. Provider `429`/`503` responses are hand
led with `Retry-After` or jittered backoff and never surface as fatal.
## Where it lives
The composer toolbar shows a small `⏱` trigger immediately before the model selector. Click it to op
en the limits menu of the session's current model. Expand **Request limit** or **Token limit** with
`+`/`−` and type per-second / per-minute / per-hour / per-day values. `0`, an empty field, or `unlim
ited` means no limit; token fields accept `k`/`m` suffixes (e.g. `500k`). The field commits on Enter
ns no limit; token fields accept `k`/`m` suffixes (e.g. `500k`). The field commits on Enter or blur.
While the model waits for capacity the trigger shows `⏸` plus a countdown (`4 s · 11 111/s`). Change
s apply immediately — no restart.
## Per-model
Limits belong to one model only. The header includes a model picker listing every model that has a p
olicy plus every model the session catalog advertises, so you can set limits for models other than t
he currently selected one.
## Cascade
Bounded windows must stay non-decreasing: `second ≤ minute ≤ hour ≤ day`. Raising a smaller window l
ifts bounded windows below it; lowering a larger window pulls bounded smaller windows above it. Sett
ing a field to unlimited never moves others.
## Idle mode
Over-limit requests queue in arrival order, consume no tokens, and arm exactly one timer for the mom
ent capacity frees. The same unchanged request resumes automatically — no user action. A request lar
ger than the whole window waits for an empty window and is flagged in the menu and log. Cancelling c
leans up timers; tools and non-model work are unaffected.
## Persistence & config
Limits live in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` under id `model-rate-limit`; counters are stored ato
mically in `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/.dsh/model-rate-limit/state.json` with one row per live second. A model
absent from the config is unlimited and costs one map lookup — no timer, no counter write, no clock
t from the config is unlimited and costs one map lookup — no timer, no counter write, no clock read.
## Install
Install bundle `dsh-llm-model-rate-limit` from the Plugin Manager (point it at this repo). A profile
restart is required to load the client bundle; the Plugin Manager shows *Installed — restart to app
uired to load the client bundle; the Plugin Manager shows *Installed — restart to apply* until then.
## Verification
130 tests (cascade, window boundaries, FIFO/idle queue, 429 recovery, persistence and clock jumps, H
TTP surface, mock provider), lint and typecheck clean.
## Limitations

- Limits are process-local; several DSH processes on one provider account don't share a budget.
- Co
unters are rolling-window, not a durable ledger — a crash between flushes loses up to one flush inte

rval of accounting.
- Aliased model ids are treated as independent models.
